subject: How to figure out clusters based on the spatial random field?

messages.subject: How to figure out clusters based on the spatial random field?
parts: I have got the spatial random field in a lake, and wonder how to distinguish the number of clusters based on the random field. Visually, it displays 4 clusters. Can I run cluster analysis to distinguish the number of locations of clusters? Does it make sense?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: How to figure out clusters based on the spatial random field?
parts: On 14 Feb 2017, at 19:37, Ruby Ji <crysta...@gmail.com> wrote:

Yes. It seems to show four different color pattern in the plot (someone might say there are 5, 6 or more). So to confirm, I want to do a cluster analysis. However, I am not sure if it is appropriate to do such analysis on the random field, because it is a model output.

I see no standout patterns at all.
To me it just looks like the field starts with low values (blue) in the left end, increase toward the middle (red) and decreases again toward the upper right (dark blue).  Be aware that the colour scale you chose has a tendency to give a visual impression of sharp features where none exist in reality. (No that's even if you increase the number of discrete colour levels.) Try using a visually smooth colour map instead, e.g. grayscale or other monochromatic map.

This blog, and other entries and links from it, is useful reading:
https://betterfigures.org/2014/11/18/end-of-the-rainbow/
